requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service on node1
requirements.summary: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service created with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started via systemctl; status confirmed active with a tracked main PID.

requirements.requirement: Service reachable and serving correctly before any disruption
requirements.summary: curl to /health and / returned valid JSON, and the main PID's oom_score_adj was confirmed as -1000 prior to the OOM test.

requirements.requirement: System is driven out of memory by a memory-hungry process
requirements.summary: Swap disabled to make OOM reproducible; a detached hog.py process grew RSS to ~410MB anon-rss until the kernel invoked the OOM killer, confirmed via dmesg.

requirements.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
requirements.summary: dmesg kernel task table at the OOM event shows inventory-api (PID 1993) at oom_score_adj -1000 (protected) versus the hog (PID 2372) at oom_score_adj 0 with the highest oom score (803); the kernel explicitly killed the hog process, sparing inventory-api.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving during and after the OOM event
requirements.summary: systemctl is-active and curl /health, / checks succeeded both while the hog was consuming memory and immediately after the kill and cleanup, with swap restored to its original state.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with full pre/post transition
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (151c4aa9...) and healthy service state captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; post-restart boot_id (50a5097c...) differs and is corroborated by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot; inventory-api auto-started, active, enabled, serving correct responses, and oom_score_adj=-1000 persisted.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct evidence: inventory-api is deployed as a systemd-managed, OOM-protected service on node1, a genuine kernel-level OOM event was reproduced showing the kernel killing the memory hog (oom_score_adj 0) while sparing inventory-api (oom_score_adj -1000), and the service kept serving throughout and after the event. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also fully satisfied, with a boot-identity change and full service/config recovery cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only notable issue is a small piece of unremoved test residue (/opt/testing/hog.py) left on the node, which is minor but not accounted for in the executor's otherwise thorough cleanup.
limitations: The /opt/testing directory and hog.py script created for the OOM test were not explicitly confirmed removed by any executor command or lifecycle snapshot (lifecycle temp-file tracking is scoped to /tmp only, so this residue is not visible in the fixed diff).
Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before_prepare and after_executor lifecycle snapshots, so package-manager consistency cannot be independently verified.
The restart protocol was demonstrated on the only managed node (node1); no cross-node comparison was possible or required given the single-node topology.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command review found one bounded, fully-reverted mutation and one piece of leftover residue. (1) swapoff -a / swapon -a (cmd-ce7629b196f64c9c, cmd-cd0cf30ce7234ec5) temporarily disabled swap to make the global OOM condition reproducible quickly; this is a system-wide but low-risk and fully-restored mutation with a clear causal link to producing the required OOM demonstration. (2) /opt/testing/hog.py and the /opt/testing directory were created (cmd-34bc2eba10b44d47) to run the memory-hog test process, but unlike /tmp/hog.log and /tmp/hog.pid (explicitly removed in cmd-cd0cf30ce7234ec5), no command removes /opt/testing/hog.py or its parent directory — this is executor-caused residue left on node1 with no evidence of cleanup. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were observed; the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed-services entries and only the expected new inventory-api listener on 8080.
